recipes.name: Poppy Seed Chicken Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 sleeve buttery round crackers (such as Ritz®), crushed
1 teaspoon poppy seeds, or more if desired
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Place chicken breasts into a large pot; cover with water and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium, cover, and simmer until chicken is no longer pink in the center, about 20 minutes. Drain; shred chicken with two forks.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Mix crackers, melted butter, and poppy seeds together in a large bowl until combined; set aside.
Stir condensed soup and sour cream together in a medium bowl; pour 1/2 of the mixture into a 9-inch square baking dish.
Add shredded chicken in an even layer.
Top with remaining soup mixture. Sprinkle with Cheddar cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until cheese has melted and the sauce is bubbly, 25 to 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Poppy Seed Chicken Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This easy poppy seed chicken casserole has layers of creamy sauce, tender shredded chicken, and cheese, topped with buttery crackers and poppy seeds.

video.description: When it comes to classic casseroles, poppyseed chicken makes anyone’s best-of list. In this video, learn how to make a delicious version of this Southern favorite that will have your friends and family asking for more. This quick and easy dish comes together fast, and it doesn’t take many ingredients. It makes the perfect choice for those hurried weeknight dinners, and you can even freeze it to save for later.

review.reviewBody: This is the chicken casserole I grew up with, except we leave out the cheese. One tip from years of making it for those of you who work outside the home full time: put the boneless skinless chicken breasts (frozen works great) in the crockpot with a cup of water on low all day... then you don't have to boil the chicken when you get home and it is so tender and easy to shred with two forks. Also, I used just 2 Tablespoons butter; it works fine for a sleeve of buttery crackers.

We’ve loved this dish for years but ours has no cheese. I also assemble it differently. I mix the chicken into the combined sour cream and soup. First into my casserole dish is a layer of prepared chicken flavor rice a roni. Next is frozen broccoli florets, steamed in microwave . Then all the chicken mixture, and then topped with the crackers, butter and poppy seeds. Yummy and a complete meal!

I make this all the time. I double the crackers, I do 3/4 C melted butter, family size can of cream of chicken, and 5-6 chicken breast, and 1.5 or 2x the sour cream. I don't layer the same way. I mix chicken and cream sauce together, pour half in my casserole dish, sprinkle half the cheese, dump in the rest of the chicken mixture, then the rest of the cheese. Then cracker topping goes on last. I also love poppy so I put more in the cream sauce and less in the topping. We love to serve this over white rice! It's a household staple.

I just mix everything together and put it in the casserole dish. I add a bit of onion powder, garlic powder & poppy seeds to the mix. Top with the cracker mixture. I also sometimes split it between 2 smaller dishes (without crackers) & freeze one.

I have been making this for years, it's always been a family favorite! But I have never put any cheddar cheese in it. I put 1 can of cream of chicken & 1 can of cream of celery soup & mix it with the sour cream and add the shredded chicken & mix all together and place in a 13x9 pan. Top with the poppy seed & crushed crackers. They gobble it up!

Absolutely a good recipe. I did follow it but I want to provide a couple clarifications. With the world and changing packaging . So for one sleeve of buttery round crackers please use 32 to 36 crackers. Also the recipe calls for four skinless boneless chicken breast tabs. Mine were very very large so I would suggest quantifying this by ounces but I don’t know how many. I also made a mistake when I put the recipe together instead of layering the sauce and then the chicken in the sauce, I mixed it all together and it was absolutely fantastic. Those of you that have a KitchenAid mixer I just threw the hot cooked chicken breasts in that to shred it and then I threw in the soups and the sour cream and it made it very easy. Excellent dish. We had it with rice

After reading suggestions from other raters, I added sautéed onion and garlic and tossed in some baby portabella mushrooms. I mixed that in with the shredded chicken and put all of that on the bottom of the pan. I topped it off with the soup & sour cream mixture, omitted the cheese and finished with the cracker crumbs. It was really good.

I’m trying Greek yogurt for half of the sour cream. We’ll see how it turns out. Also, I’m omitting the cheddar cheese and preparing the chicken by cooking it in small chunks. I then mixed the soup, sour cream, Greek yogurt, poppy seeds together and poured it over the chicken along with a bag of frozen mixed vegetables which I had warmed up with the chicken. I bake that mixture for half an hour and top it with the cracker and melted butter mixture and bake for 10 more minutes.

I made this recipe and forgot to put in the 2nd layer of the soup mixture over the chicken. It was too late when I noticed AFTER I put the Cheddar cheese on. Wasn't sure how it would turn out, but it turned out great! You can also cut this recipe down in 1/2 to put in an 8X8 baking dish because I was only feeding 2 of us. I also used SHARP cheddar cheese because that was all I had and I liked it better than regular cheddar cheese! Will make again and again...

This really is a good recipe....needed pepper for us. The old school recipes do not call for shredded cheese so i do not usually use it. Cut the butter in half and add a can of cream of celery soup for more flavor and sauce for the chicken (and rice if you serve this on top of it)) Also, don't add the poppy seeds to the cracker mix, add it to your condensed soup mix instead so you get more of the flavor and look of poppy seed chicken. Sprinkle some on top of course before baking. Still, this one is a keeper over-all.

I mix the condensed cream of chicken soup, sour cream, shredded Cheddar cheese together and then add chopped onion, cubed potatoes and vegetables to the mixture before topping. We love this on mashed potatoes or biscuits.

So easy and delicious. Everyone loved it! I used Rotisseries chicken which saved a lot of work and time. My grocery store sells day-old shredded rotisserie chicken. You can't beat it. However, if I wanted to double it, what size pan do I need? Would a 9 X 13 be right?
My family loved it!

Our DIL made this dish by request (sans poppyseeds) for our granddaughter's 16th birthday. I stood and watched her put the dish together. It was delicious. One comment: When I asked the DIL what she was going to do with the water in which the chicken breasts were poached, she said that she was going to throw it away. When I asked to taste it, I found it was a delicious tasting broth, to which I added S&P and later a few green scallion bits and some parsley left over from the salad prep for the same meal. Our son and I ended up drinking that hot chicken broth while waiting for the celebration meal to begin. Since the DIL served the dish over rice, that poaching water could also have been used to cook the rice.
This was so terrific! My husband is really picky and won't eat something twice. He ate it three times voluntarily. He ever spread it on a cooked porkchop steak as a topping. Winner!
I like to add peas to the casserole. It’s yummy.

I love this casseroles! I learned how to make it from the ladies at church when we’d have socials. One thing I will note. If you work out of the house and in a drug free workplace, I would leave out the poppyseeds. They tend to give false drug readings. My husband is a pilot so I definitely leave out the poppyseeds. But I think I will try a couple of dashes of poultry seasoning this time.
I added a couple dashes of poultry seasoning for extra flavor. I always serve on rice or noodles.
Easy to put together and I had some broccoli leftover and added them very yummy.
My whole family loved this recipe.......with 9 people, that is hard to do in our house. Only comment from the family was it needed to have a little more sauce. This is definitely a "make again".
